Authentix dashboard — organisation-specific security scan instructions.

Next.js App Router frontend on Vercel for a B2B multi-tenant certificate platform.
It talks to a separate Fastify backend through a BFF proxy. Auth is Supabase OTP
only — there is NO password anywhere in this product; signup and login both issue
an 8-digit emailed code.

Weight these real, product-specific shapes heavily.

1. THE BFF PROXY IS THE TRUST BOUNDARY.
   app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts forwards browser requests to the backend.
   Look hard for:
   - Any path or header the client controls being forwarded without validation
     (path traversal into an unintended backend route, header injection,
     smuggling an organization id or role the user should not have).
   - Server-only credentials or service keys reaching the client bundle.
   - The proxy attaching auth on behalf of a request it has not authorised.

2. SECRETS IN THE CLIENT BUNDLE.
   Anything named NEXT_PUBLIC_* is shipped to the browser. A Supabase SERVICE or
   SECRET key, a backend worker secret, or a payment secret behind that prefix is
   a critical finding. Check for server-only values imported into a Client
   Component, or leaking through props from a Server Component.

3. THE SSR AUTHORISATION GATE.
   app/dashboard/org/[slug]/layout.tsx gates every dashboard route with an
   HttpOnly-cookie check plus a server-to-server call to /auth/access-context.
   This runs during SSR, before any browser JavaScript. Report anything that
   weakens it: a route rendered outside the gated segment, a client-side-only
   check standing in for it, or a cached/stale authorisation decision.
   Note: the org slug is in the URL and is user-controlled. Membership must be
   verified server-side on every request, never inferred from the slug.

4. OTP AND SESSION HANDLING.
   - Auth tokens must stay in HttpOnly cookies, never localStorage or
     sessionStorage, and never in a URL query parameter.
   - Sign-in codes must not be logged, echoed in a response, or exposed in a
     redirect. We shipped a defect where the signup OTP went out as a magic link
     instead of a code (GARDEN-27) — treat anything that turns a one-time code
     into a clickable URL as security-relevant.
   - Open redirects on the post-login return path.

5. XSS AND UNTRUSTED RENDERING.
   dangerouslySetInnerHTML, any HTML built from certificate data, template field
   values, recipient names, or organisation names. Recipient data is customer-
   supplied and reaches template rendering — treat every field as untrusted.

6. SILENT FAILURE ON AN AUTH PATH.
   A swallowed error during bootstrap, session refresh or the access-context call
   can leave a user in a wrong-tenant or partially-authorised state with nothing
   surfaced. We shipped exactly that (GARDEN-53): auto-bootstrap failures were
   swallowed entirely. Treat a silently-caught failure on an auth or org
   resolution path as a security finding, not a code-quality nit.

CROSS-REPO NOTE: the backend enforces tenant isolation with an organization_id
filter taken from the verified JWT. This frontend must never be the only thing
enforcing that, and must never pass an organization id up from user input as
though it were authoritative.

Report authentication bypass, cross-tenant data exposure and client-side secret
leakage at the highest severity you have.
